2010_002_030210_regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held Tuesday, March 2, 2010, at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It combines a recognition resolution for State Senator John Pappageorge and State Representative Marty Knollenberg over the vetoed 20j funding, a consent agenda with February minutes and a copy paper bid, curriculum reports on a grades 6-12 English textbook adoption and READ 180, and business items covering artificial turf, tennis courts, SMART boards, a Sodexo contract addendum and unfunded mandates. Its centerpiece is the 2010/2011 budget reduction plan against a projected $11.7 million deficit, totaling $6,243,270 in adjustments.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, March 2, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except July and August.

**Recognition**
A resolution thanks State Senator John Pappageorge and State Representative Marty Knollenberg for advocating reinstatement of 20j funding. Governor Granholm signed a school aid bill on October 19, 2009 line-item vetoing 20j for Troy and students in 40 other Michigan communities, cutting Troy funding by $248.18 per pupil, or nearly $3 million annually, which the resolution says broke the hold-harmless promise made to Troy voters under Proposal A in 1994.

**Consent Agenda**
Minutes of the February 3, 2010 regular meeting; minutes of the February 9, 2010 workshop; and award of the copy paper bid to Midland Paper for $40,633.15 from the 2009-10 General Fund (Bid Award #9659, opened February 19, 2010; 19 bidders invited, 12 responded, one "No Bid").

**February 3, 2010 minutes (excerpt)**
President Underwood convened at 7:00 p.m. with members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo and Superintendent Fowler. Stuart Redpath received a plaque for district-wide North Central accreditation and Jasen Witt accepted MASPA's 2009 "Best Practices in Human Resources" award. Actions: 10-012 consent agenda (7-0); 10-013 closing Athens and Troy High Schools to open enrollment for 2010/2011 except up to 25 ninth graders from the Troy High area (7-0); 10-014 an Athens High School security management system to MCMI for $66,800.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (7-0); 10-015 the 2009/2010 budget amendment; 10-016 closed session on negotiations. Adjourned 9:38 p.m.

**Curriculum Reports**
English textbook recommendation, grades 6-12: McDougal Littell Literature, 2008, presented by Jane McKenney (Baker) and Christina Vettraino (Troy High); adoption spread over two years, grades 9-12 in 2010-2011 and grades 6-8 in 2011-2012. READ 180 report by coach Jan Hagland with teachers Renee Anderson, Lauryn Mordarski, Kathryn Taylor and Wendy Wilcox-Noronha.

**Business Bids and Contracts**

| Item | Vendor | Amount | Fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Artificial turf replacement (#9651) | General Sports Venue | $711,137.00 | 2004 Capital Projects |
| Tennis court updates (#9652) | Best Asphalt | $228,690.00 | 2004 Capital Projects |
| SMART interactive white boards (#9657) | Smart Ed Services | $418,964.50 | 2004 Capital Projects |

Also considered: a Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract addendum assigning Gayle Moran as General Manager effective January 18, 2010, and a resolution backing the Legislative Commission on Statutory Mandates' December 2009 final report on unfunded mandates under the Headlee Amendment.

**Budget Reduction Plan for 2010/2011**
Michael Adamczyk reported a projected $11.7 million deficit, with further state revenue cuts of up to $300 per pupil expected, a 2.47 percent retirement rate increase, insurance and step increases, and reduced county-wide special education revenue (PA 18). Total proposed reductions for 2010/11 are $6,243,270, with 22.4 non-certified FTE and 37.0 certified (TEA) FTE reductions. Item 8.G asks the Board to authorize approximately $6 million in adjustments plus a draw on existing fund equity.

| 2011-2012 | $8 million | $3.6 million | $9.4 million |

**Meeting.** Board agenda for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, March 2, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August.

**Recognition (2.A).** A resolution honors State Senator John Pappageorge and State Representative Marty Knollenberg. It recites that Governor Granholm signed a school aid bill on October 19, 2009 with a line-item veto of 20j funding for Troy and students in 40 other Michigan communities, cutting Troy funding by $248.18 per pupil, or nearly $3 million annually, beyond reductions already targeted at every Michigan district, and that the veto broke the promise made to Troy voters under Proposal A in 1994 that the community would be held harmless. Both lawmakers authored and voted for measures to return the funds; the resolution urges them to vote against any school aid bill without full 20j reinstatement. Signed this second day of March, 2010.

**Consent agenda and February 3, 2010 minutes.** Items A-C are the February 3, 2010 meeting minutes, the February 9, 2010 workshop minutes, and the copy paper bid award. On February 3 President Underwood convened at 7:00 p.m. with Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Adamczyk, Machesky, McAvoy, Mull, Papasian, Stromayer and Witt, and approximately 18 additional audience members. Stuart Redpath, chair of the district-wide NCA process, received a plaque for accreditation by the Advanced Accreditation Commission; the Troy Academy of Learning Leaders (TALL) earned the 2009 "Best Practices in Human Resources" award from the Michigan Association of School Personnel Administrators (MASPA), presented to Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent-Human Resources, at the MASPA annual conference in December. Frank Barket, a Baker Middle School parent, asked about attending Athens High School while living in the Troy High attendance area; Jennifer Lee raised concerns about the T.O.T.S. program moving from Costello Elementary School to the Niles Center.
Motion 10-012 (Hauff/Fleming) approved minutes of the January 19, 2010 organizational meeting and the January 19 and January 22, 2010 retreats, 7-0. Jennifer Gottlieb, science and math coordinator, reported on the February 1, 2010 live downlink with International Space Station crew, Troy being one of only six districts in the nation to host one. Stuart Redpath and Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, presented a parent survey conducted November 10-23, 2009. Motion 10-013 (Pochodylo/Edmunds) closed Athens and Troy High Schools to open enrollment for 2010/2011 except not more than 25 ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area and siblings in grades 9-11, 7-0. Motion 10-014 (Miletti/Philippart) awarded an Athens High School security management system to MCMI for $66,800.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, 7-0. Motion 10-015 (Edmunds/Philippart) amended the 2009/2010 appropriations: General Fund $136,562,590; Special Revenue Funds 7,614,554; Debt Service Funds 18,749,640; Capital Projects Fund 5,032,861; Internal Service Fund 720,000. Michael Adamczyk gave a five-year budget forecast and Tim McAvoy, Director-Community Relations, outlined the budget communications plan. Athens student representative Enxhi Xhafa reported nearly $3,000 raised for Haiti relief. Motion 10-016 (Philippart/Edmunds) entered closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), roll call 7-0; closed at 8:38 p.m., reconvened 9:37 p.m., adjourned 9:38 p.m. Submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary.

**February 9, 2010 workshop.** Vice President Miletti convened at 6:00 p.m. at the Administrative Center with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Philippart and Pochodylo; Underwood absent; Superintendent Fowler and administrators Adamczyk, Keeling, Machesky, McAvoy and Witt attended with one community member. Topics: public communication, diversity initiative update, review of the 2010/2011 budget, and Michigan Department of Education budget transparency. Adjourned 8:50 p.m.

**Copy paper (5.C).** Bid Award #9659. Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, wrote Michael M. Adamczyk on February 23, 2010 that bids were opened February 19, 2010; invitations went to 19 potential bidders with 12 responding, one a "No Bid." Award recommended to Midland Paper at $40,633.15 from the 2009-10 General Fund. Purchasing Department: 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077.

**English textbook recommendation, grades 6-12 (7.A).** Teachers began meeting in spring of 2008-2009 to define college and workplace readiness and a learning progression with skills benchmarks for language conventions. Budget restrictions spread adoption over two years: grades 9-12 in 2010-2011, grades 6-8 in 2011-2012, with a textbook for each student plus home resources on CD and/or online. Reported by Jane McKenney (Baker Middle School) and Christina Vettraino (Troy High School). Texts examined: Elements of Literature, 2009, Holt McDougal; McDougal Littell Literature, 2008, McDougal Littell; Prentice Hall Literature: Timeless Voices, Timeless Themes, 2008, Prentice Hall; and Glencoe Literature, 2009, Glencoe. Recommended publisher: McDougal Littell Literature, 2008, citing authors Carol Tomlinson, Robert Marzano, Janet Allen, Yvette Jackson, Jim Burke and Carol Booth Olson, a Grammar for Writing textbook and teacher resource CDs. Criteria included State of Michigan grade level essential questions and ACT College Readiness Standards. The selection committee drew members from Baker, Boulan, Larson and Smith middle schools, Athens and Troy High Schools and Niles Community High School, among them Betsy Kennedy, Colin Quinn, Jackie Morris, Omar Hakim, Jill Kelly, Sue Baran, Chris Tolen and Jo O'Brien.

**READ 180 (7.B).** Scholastic's READ 180 has been used in Troy middle schools since 2007-2008. Retired Troy elementary principal and reading specialist Jan Hagland coaches the program; teachers are Renee Anderson (Boulan Park), Lauryn Mordarski (Smith), Kathryn "Katie" Taylor (Baker) and Wendy Wilcox-Noronha (Larson). It was piloted one semester in 2006-2007 at Larson and Baker, adopted in all four middle schools in 2007-2008, fully implemented in 2008-2009, with 2009-2010 as Year 3. Lexile measures come from the Scholastic Reading Inventory (SRI). The presentation states over 70 percent of current 7th and 8th grade students serviced in READ 180 beginning in 2008-2009 maintained, improved, or significantly improved their Reading MEAP scores in 2009, notes such programs typically target the bottom 20 percent of a grade level, and cites Scholastic's benchmark of at least 75 Lexile points of growth per year in a September 2009 to February 2010 report. Students Mataya, Alex, Alexis and Mike are quoted; guest speaker Brennan Ferrilla is a 9th grader at Athens High School and READ 180 graduate.

**Bids (8.A-8.C).** Artificial turf replacement, Bid Award #9651: bids opened February 4, 2010 for turf at Athens and Troy High Schools, six registered plan holders with nine bidders responding, none "No Bid"; reviewed with Bruce Lemons of Foresite Design and Ken Miller, Director of Operations; award to General Sports Venue at $711,137.00 including Alternates #1 and #3, from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (memo February 18, 2010). Tennis court updates, Bid Award #9652, Troy High Tennis Court Reconstruction: bids opened February 4, 2010, 11 registered plan holders all bidding, one rejected for omitting the state-required Familial Disclosure Statement; reviewed with Bruce Lemons and Mondo Belardi, Director of Maintenance; award to Best Asphalt at $228,690.00 from the same fund (memo February 12, 2010). SMART interactive white boards, Bid Award #9657: Scott Bryan, Director of Technology (Technology Resource Center, 4420 Livernois, 248-823-5090), issued the bid February 3, 2010; a voluntary pre-bid conference was held February 9 with four potential bidders; bids opened February 17, 2010, two received, post-bid meetings February 19, both compliant; nine bidders invited, three responded, one "No Bid." Recommended low bid: Smart Ed Services, a division of Cleveland Corporate Services, Inc., base bid $418,964.50 for 100 Board packages, funded from excess bond issue funds as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Superintendent: Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D.

**Food service addendum (8.D) and unfunded mandates (8.E).** On May 19, 2009 the Board approved contracting with Sodexo Management, Inc. for food service; an addendum reviewed and approved by the Michigan Department of Education assigns Gayle Moran as General Manager effective January 18, 2010. The unfunded mandates resolution recites the November 1978 Headlee Amendment (Article IX, Section 29), effective December 23, 1978; the Legislative Commission on Statutory Mandates created by P.A. 98 of 2007 as amended by P.A. 356 of 2008; work with the Citizens Research Council, Michigan School Business Officials and Michigan Association of School Administrators; a June 2009 interim report finding the State never enacted enabling legislation; and a December 2009 final report (slides dated December 31, 2009) recommending Court of Appeals review by a special master ruling within six months. Slides add that the Commission was created in October 2007 while the state income tax was being raised to 4.35 percent, cite 31 years of ignoring the 1978 amendment and 30 years of ignoring Public Act 101 of 1979, and note the Supreme Court required the State to pay $1 billion to schools in 1997-98 after Durant 1 and Durant 2. The Board approves release of the resolution to the Governor, Legislators and Supreme Court, certified in Oakland County this 2nd day of March 2010.

**Budget reduction plan for 2010/2011 (8.F).** Presented by Michael Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services. Causes: continued flat or reduced school funding since 2002 and severe 2009-2010 revenue cuts, comprising elimination of 20j at -$248.18 per pupil ($3 million) and a per pupil cut of -$165 per pupil ($1.98 million). Prior response: $51.7 million in adjustments since 2002, of which adjustments were $33.1 million and fund equity $18.6 million; 2009-2010 expenditure cuts of $7.6 million; more than $1 million in mid-year department cuts; 2.5 percent compensation reductions for administrative and non-represented employees; a $2 million deficit covered through fund equity; and privatization of custodial, grounds, transportation and food services for approximately $3.1 million in annual savings. Current position: a projected $11.7 million deficit, further state cuts of up to $300 per pupil, step increases, an insurance increase, a 2.47 percent retirement rate increase, contractual obligations, and reduced county-wide special education revenue (PA 18). The long-range plan lists 2010-2011 adjustments of $6.2 million, fund equity use of $5.5 million and a balance of $13 million; 2011-2012 adjustments of $8 million, fund equity of $3.6 million and a balance of $9.4 million; and 2012-2013 adjustments of $7.5 million, fund equity of ($673,210) and a balance of $10.0 million. Informational meetings were set for March 8, 10 and 15, 2010, 6:30-8:00 p.m. at Athens High School.
Proposed adjustments, (E) expenditure or (R) revenue: Schools of Choice expansion in grades K-1 ($7,950 x 90) (R) $715,500; eliminate elementary sections by raising class sizes to contractual limits (E) $683,327; maximize high school class sizes (E) $569,439; 10.2% reduction for guest teachers and non-staff coaches, TSS daily rate from $98 to $88 (E) $289,334; fewer guest teachers for professional development (E) $261,724; pay-to-participate athletic fees from $50 middle school and $100 high school to $100 and $200, family maximum $300 to $400, club/intramural fees $35 to $50 (R) $250,000; Enviro-Clean cleaning schedule (E) $200,000; 3.0 custodial coordinators (E) $175,219; step savings from laid-off teachers (E) $142,358; 4.2 ELL tutors (E) $139,907; assistant high school principals 0.5 per school (E) $127,476; technology budget (E) $122,094; 2.0 elementary PACE teachers (E) $113,888; 1.2 ELL coordinators (E) $113,888; health care aides through Temporary Staff Services, Inc. (E) $104,039; advertising via Alternative Revenue Development (R) $100,000; privatized grounds services (E) $96,322; restructured 5th grade music (E) $85,416; Spanish in grades 1 and 2 (E) $85,416; theater budget (E) $80,000; 0.5 middle school clerk per building (E) $77,493; high school clerical restructuring (E) $77,493; maintenance budget (E) $75,000; elementary clerical staffing by 2.1 FTE (E) $73,028; 2 bus runs (E) $68,879; 1.2 curriculum coordinators (E) $68,333; postponed IAE counselor (E) $66,356; 1.0 social worker (E) $56,944; Algebraic Thinking coach (E) $50,000; purchased elementary science kits (E) $46,935; middle school media specialists 0.2 per building (E) $45,555; high school parking fee $20 to $40 (R) $40,000; 4.0 counselors $227,776; Community Ed fund equity transfer (R) $300,000; consolidating non-instructional services with another district (R) $150,000; $3.00 freshmen sports admission (R) $15,600; facility usage fees up 20% (R) $15,290. Total reductions for 2010/11: $6,243,270, with FTE reductions of 22.4 non-certified staff (administration, TESPA, TESA, non-represented) and 37.0 certified staff (TEA), which the packet notes is not indicative of total positions affected.

**Authorization to implement (8.G).** The resolution states the district has made more than $50 million in budget adjustments since 2002 and faces an estimated $11.7 million deficit in 2010-2011, and that the Board expects to pursue a three-year plan using fund equity and adjustments protecting core academic programs. It authorizes the administration to implement approximately $6 million in budget adjustments and draw on existing fund equity, and commits the Board to continue working with community, parents, staff, bargaining units and state lawmakers.
